name: Black Bean, Butternut Squash & Jalapeño Enchiladas

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, and peel each butternut squash; halve and remove seeds with a spoon. Small dice squash and place in a large bowl; set aside.
Peel and small dice onions; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the squash.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ medium yellow onions
6 cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, and quarter jalapeños lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices to the pot; cook, stirring occasionally, until squash is fork-tender, 8-10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
chili powder
salt
garlic powder
onion powder
¾ tsp cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, measure oil into a medium saucepan and place over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, whisk in the flour; continuing to whisk, cook the flour until lightly golden, about 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in tomato sauce, broth, and spices. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until thickened, 5-6 minutes. Remove enchilada sauce from heat and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (8 oz) cans tomato sauce
18 fl oz (2 ¼ cups) chicken or vegetable broth
chili powder
garlic powder
onion powder
salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans. Grate mozzarella.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (15 oz) cans black beans
1 (8 oz) block mozzarella cheese

instructions.primary_message: Add beans, half the cheese (reserving the rest for later), and yogurt to the pot with the veggies. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
Spread a thin layer of the enchilada sauce over the bottom of a large baking dish; set remaining sauce aside.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide vegetable mixture evenly between them; roll up and place, seam-side down, in the baking dish. Top with remaining sauce and cheese.
Place enchiladas in the oven and bake until the cheese is melted, 10-12 minutes.
To serve, divide enchiladas between plates and enjoy!
